prompt: compare the sales from last year q4 with this year q1
title: Q4 vs Q1 Sales Comparison
summary: Compare sales performance from last year’s Q4 with this year’s Q1. Highlight changes in revenue, growth or decline, and any notable trends.
executed_sql_queries: SELECT MIN(order_date) AS min_order_date, MAX(order_date) AS max_order_date FROM retail.orders;

SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month_start, SUM(oi.total_amount) AS monthly_sales
FROM retail.orders o
JOIN retail.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN retail.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE o.order_date >= DATE_TRUNC('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 quarter'
  AND o.order_date < DATE_TRUNC('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '1 quarter'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

WITH bounds AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '3 months' AS last_year_start,
    DATE_TRUNC('year', CURRENT_DATE) AS this_year_start,
    DATE_TRUNC('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '3 months' AS this_q2_start
)
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month_start,
  SUM(oi.total_amount) AS monthly_sales
FROM retail.orders o
JOIN retail.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN retail.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
CROSS JOIN bounds b
WHERE (
    o.order_date >= b.last_year_start AND o.order_date < b.this_year_start
  )
  OR (
    o.order_date >= b.this_year_start AND o.order_date < b.this_q2_start
  )
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

SELECT DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_date) AS quarter_start, s.store_name, SUM(oi.total_amount) AS sales
FROM retail.orders o
JOIN retail.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN retail.stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
WHERE o.order_date >= DATE_TRUNC('quarter', DATE_TRUNC('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 year' + INTERVAL '9 months')
  AND o.order_date < DATE_TRUNC('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '3 months'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

components.content:
Executive summary: Across the 8 accessible stores, total sales increased from $1,949,295.82 in last year’s Q4 to $2,640,785.38 in this year’s Q1.

  • Absolute change: +$691,489.56
  • Percentage change: +35.5%

Quarter trend: Q4 monthly sales were relatively steady at $600,021.19 in October, $599,552.89 in November, and $626,893.94 in December. Q1 started stronger, with $725,969.01 in January and a peak of $763,329.92 in February, before easing to $650,763.49 in March.

Store-level drivers: Growth was led by the largest channels:

  • Zava Retail Bellevue: $338,878.82 → $402,601.46 (+$63,722.64)
  • Zava Retail Seattle: $507,381.28 → $595,007.26 (+$87,625.98)
  • Zava Retail Online: $521,203.76 → $596,115.47 (+$74,911.71)
  • Zava Retail Tacoma: $233,059.99 → $283,257.80 (+$50,197.81)

Notable smaller-store movement: Redmond rose from $43,556.97 to $62,078.40 (+$18,521.43), Spokane from $93,167.97 to $107,215.14 (+$14,047.17), and Kirkland from $25,413.55 to $32,075.68 (+$6,662.13). Everett was essentially flat, slipping slightly from $63,805.68 to $61,711.21 (-$2,094.47).

Takeaway: Q1 outperformed Q4 by a wide margin, with the uplift concentrated in Seattle, Online, Bellevue, and Tacoma. The business entered the new year with stronger demand across the core stores, while March’s pullback suggests a need to watch whether February was a seasonal peak or the start of a higher run-rate.

title.text: Total Sales Comparison: Last Year Q4 vs This Year Q1
Monthly Sales Trend: Q4 Last Year to Q1 This Year

components.content:
Head Office view: sales increased from $1,748,990.85 in Q4 2025 to $2,053,809.42 in Q1 2026, an absolute gain of $304,818.57 and a 17.4% increase.

  • Monthly trend: Q4 2025 was relatively flat across the quarter ($600,021.19 in Oct, $599,552.89 in Nov, then $626,893.94 in Dec). Q1 2026 stepped up sharply in Jan and Feb ($725,969.01 and $763,329.92), before easing in Mar to $650,763.49.
  • Biggest month: February 2026 was the peak month at $763,329.92, up $163,777.03 vs Dec 2025 (+26.1%).
  • Store drivers: the largest contributors to the quarter-over-quarter lift were Bellevue (+$63,722.64), Seattle (+$87,625.98), Online (+$74,911.71), Tacoma (+$50,197.81), and Redmond (+$18,521.43).
  • Notable offsets: Everett declined slightly by $2,094.47, while Kirkland grew modestly by $6,662.13 and Spokane by $14,047.17.
  • Mix insight: Online remained the largest channel/store in both periods, rising from $521,203.76 to $596,115.47 and accounting for roughly 29.0% of Q1 sales.
